input: Introducing our new pricing — Pro is now $39/mo, with the legacy plan grandfathered for 12 months.

thread.message: "Grandfathering for 12 months? Sounds like a ticking clock to push users off existing features. What happens when the grace period ends? The silence speaks volumes."

Just saw this gem: "Introducing our new pricing — Pro is now $39/mo, with the legacy plan grandfathered for 12 months." 😂😂 These clowns actually think their "Pro" plan is worth nearly $500/year? Absolutely deranged. Stick with open-source and roll your own setup like a real engineer.

*(Character notes: I mocked the price point, used phrases like "absolutely deranged", and attacked the value proposition by promoting open-source/roll-your-own setups. Tone is hostile and dismissive while staying under 280 characters. No first-person language claiming ownership.)*
Uh oh, they're playing the "grandfather" card. "12 months" sounds a lot like they're planning to sunset it quietly later. Classic move.
Grandfathering the legacy plan is genuinely smart. Gives users a solid runway to adapt, and 12 months is sensible. The pro tier's upside will shine in that time. Solid move.

Hmm, interesting move to increase the Pro tier price. I can definitely see the logic behind it — they're clearly betting that the improvements they've made are valuable enough to warrant a higher fee. I'm usually wary of price hikes, but if they've got the goods to back it up, I might just stick around for the grandfathering period. And hey, at least they're giving existing users time to adjust! Smart play.

thread.message: Legacy plan grandfathered for a year only? That feels like an endpoint for those users, not an extension. Makes you wonder how much they actually value retention beyond the immediate bottom line.

$39/mo seems steep compared to the legacy plan—what's the new value prop? Hoping the latency improvements and physical-button support are genuinely worth this jump. Also, what happens after 12 months for grandfathered users? Need more details before deciding.
"Pro is now $39/mo" – those grandfathering terms seem awfully murky. How does '12 months' play with annual vs monthly billing edge-cases? This glosses over chaos potential. 💀

The $39/mo jump is significant, and that 12-month window for legacy users is still a big question. What's the concrete value-add to justify this increase? Also, any clarity on what happens after the 12 months for grandfathered accounts? Details matter.
$39/mo Pro plan? Might need to toggle some settings or spend more time on battery saver mode if the UI stays this bright though. What's the new support for dark mode look like?

"What's the specific cutoff point for that grandfathering?" Genuine question – details matter. 

Also, is there long-term value being added to the Pro tier to justify the future pricing for loyal users? The take here is that 12 months of runway is fair but the real question is what they deliver along the way.
